Usage: drive record answer --took=TOOK <ask> [<line> ...] [flags]

Record the owner's answer to an ask.

A step given here goes to the session the ask is about, at the view it stands
at now, so one command answers an ask and sends what follows from it. Refused,
it records nothing and sends nothing.

Arguments:
  <ask>                  The ask it answers, such as A3.
  <line> ...             The step as one line, typed as is, a slash command too; with --snippet, the
                         text the owner would type after the key (optional).

Flags:
      --source=SOURCE    The owner's words, or what showed the ask no longer holds.
      --took=TOOK        Whether the owner took the recommendation, amended it, handed the question
                         to someone else, or it stopped mattering (required; one of: recommended,
                         amended, delegated, moot).
      --explained        The owner needed the question explained before answering.
      --file=PATH        Send this file instead: your own request, or anything longer than a line.
      --snippet=KEY      Send the owner's TabType snippet KEY, as it resolves in the session's
                         directory.
      --hold=NAME        With a step: name what it uses that only one session may use at a time, as
                         send's --hold does.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help             Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME       Act in this batch, as drive prints its name, instead of the driver's
                         current one. It may stand anywhere on the line.
      --driver=NAME      Act in the batch this driver drives now; a chat driver's name is its
                         webhook's. It may stand anywhere on the line.

Constraints:
  At most one of --file, --snippet.

Steps:
  A step is one of:
    'one short line'        typed as is, a slash command too; an @PATH in it attaches
                            that file, as the owner's would ('/write-spec @/tmp/answers.md'),
                            except in a step queued mid-turn, where it stays a path
    --file PATH             typed as @<copy>, which attaches it, drive keeping the copy;
                            queued mid-turn, a line asks the session to read the copy
    --snippet KEY 'TEXT'    the owner's snippet for the session's directory, with the
                            step's words, TEXT, where the owner would type after it
  Text that starts with a dash goes after --, which ends the flags.
  The first step a session gets in a batch carries the owner's notice: at the head
  of its file, or attached after its line.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
